decisions.advocate: No objection to letting the Proposed outcome win and updating the one assertion in `tests/test_calc.py`, on the condition that the decision record says it supersedes change 0015's outcome "the message names `whole`".
decisions.decision: The Proposed outcome wins: the one assertion in tests/test_calc.py::test_percent_zero_whole_error_names_whole changes to "cannot express 1 as a percent of zero", nothing else in that file moves, and this supersedes change 0015's outcome that the message names `whole`; the stale test name stays as a known nit.

decisions.item: The intent's Proposed outcome and its Constraints contradict each other on
rationale: Both verdicts reach the same decision; they differ only on whether the record names the 0015 outcome it supersedes.
That claim is checkable and true: changes/0015-.../intent.md line 17 asks for a message that names `whole`, and the 0017 intent's exact new text drops it, so the same owner knowingly let it go.

No policy picks a winner between an intent's sections, but the Constraint-wins reading also breaks the intent's own bullet 5 (pytest green) unless the change ships nothing; the Outcome-wins reading breaks one constraint's letter only.

The edit replaces one exact-equality assertion with another of equal strictness in a feature-type change (tests_locked: false), so coding-standards rule 4, CLAUDE.md "fix the code, not the test" and REVIEW.md's test lock are not engaged.
The test name nit and any rename are left to the owner at the gate, as the advocate asked; the panel does not widen the edit beyond one line.
decisions.reviewer: Close the concern as decided: the Proposed outcome governs; update the one assertion at `tests/test_calc.py:28` to `"cannot express 1 as a percent of zero"`, and read the Constraint as "no test weakened or deleted", which this edit honours.
